description:
What does a burrito have to do with winning an argument? 

On Think Fast, Talk Smart's 300th episode, Matt Abrahams answers that question and a dozen more from his own production team and listeners around the world. 
In this episode, Matt covers:
• How his PREP framework makes any argument immediately convincing.
• Why there's no such thing as the "right word" and how that can actually improve word recall.
• The ABCs of how to start a speech without freezing in those first terrifying seconds.
• The insider rule for the use of jargon in communication.
• How giving feedback as a leader requires planning for emotion.
• A simple ‘game’ that makes gestures in communication feel natural.

If you could take away only one thing from this episode, it should be this: communication is a skill, and like any skill, it demands deliberate, consistent practice to master.

About Matt:
Matt Abrahams is a leading communication expert, Lecturer in Organisational Behaviour at Stanford GSB, and host of the award-winning Think Fast, Talk Smart podcast. He has coached presenters at TED, the World Economic Forum, and the UN Secretary General's office, and his online talks have garnered millions of views worldwide. He is the author of Think Faster, Talk Smarter and Speaking Up without Freaking Out — two bestselling guides to confident, spontaneous communication.

Key Quotes
• "We tend to remember concrete examples far better than high-level information." - Matt Abrahams (2:40)
• "If you reframe your anxiety as excitement, not only do you feel better, but you actually perform better." - Matt Abrahams (10:28)
• "Communication and critical thinking are intimately related. You can't communicate well without critically thinking, and you can't critically think without being able to communicate well." - Matt Abrahams (15:09)
• “Jargon monoxide - it suffocates communication." - Huggy Rao, quoted by Matt Abrahams (20:28)
